package_info.package_versions: N/A (active on site for 5 months, no versioning)
package_info.why_malicious: The Magecart skimmer is a malicious JavaScript code injected into the First Aid Beauty e-commerce website, designed to steal credit card information from users during checkout. The code is heavily obfuscated and encrypted, specifically targets US-based Windows users, and exfiltrates sensitive payment data to attacker-controlled infrastructure. This behavior is unequivocally malicious as it compromises user privacy and financial security.

execution_context.trigger: On checkout page load and during form submission
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript in the checkout page source of the First Aid Beauty website
required_permissions: Network access (to send HTTP POST requests)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Heavily obfuscated and encrypted JavaScript skimmer code
(function(){var _0xabc=...; /* obfuscated code */ ...})();
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On checkout page load and form submission, the code hooks into the payment form, intercepts credit card and payment data entered by the user, encrypts the data, and sends it via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled server, resulting in theft of payment information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code intercepts sensitive payment data from users and exfiltrates it to an external, attacker-controlled server, which is a hallmark of Magecart skimming attacks. The use of heavy obfuscation and encryption is intended to evade detection by security tools and site administrators.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should only process payment data for authorized transaction purposes and transmit it solely to trusted, PCI-compliant payment processors. This code instead sends sensitive data to an untrusted third-party domain without user consent or business justification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate payment processors may use JavaScript to collect and transmit payment data, but only to their own secure, PCI-compliant endpoints and with explicit user consent. They do not obfuscate code to hide data exfiltration to unknown domains.
key_indicators: Heavily obfuscated and encrypted JavaScript injected into checkout page
Hooks into payment/checkout form events to capture user input
Sends payment data to untrusted, attacker-controlled external domains
Targets users based on geolocation (US) and operating system (Windows)
Encrypts or encodes form data before exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is injected into the checkout page of the First Aid Beauty website.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of skimmer code in the browser of site visitors.

attack_chain.action: When a user visits the checkout page, the skimmer code executes, hooking into the payment form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Interception of payment data entered by the user.

attack_chain.action: The skimmer collects, encrypts, and exfiltrates the payment data to an attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Theft of credit card and personal information.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into checkout or payment pages
JavaScript code hooking into form submission or input events on payment forms
Unexpected network requests to untrusted or unknown domains during checkout
Encryption or encoding of form data before transmission to external endpoints
file_indicators: Inline or external JavaScript with high entropy or obfuscation in checkout page source
Unexpected <script> tags or modified JavaScript files present in the checkout page
Presence of script code that is not part of the legitimate site or payment processor
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from checkout pages to domains not associated with the legitimate business or payment processor
Outbound connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure during checkout
Exfiltration endpoints with no business relationship to the site
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor e-commerce checkout pages for injected or obfuscated JavaScript, especially scripts that hook into payment forms and send data to unknown domains. Use web application firewalls and strict content security policies to block unauthorized script execution and outbound requests. Regularly audit site JavaScript for unauthorized changes, and monitor network traffic for suspicious POST requests or exfiltration patterns to untrusted domains.
